title: Automatic Connective Selection for Interpretable Neuro-Fuzzy Rules
abstract: In evolving data streams, neuro-fuzzy systems must adapt to non-stationary distributions while preserving interpretability and numerical stability. However, most evolving fuzzy models rely on fixed logical connectives or implicitly encode logical behavior, limiting transparency and flexibility. This paper introduces the UnimNeuron, a neuro-fuzzy neuron whose antecedent connective is automatically selected from data using an order-invariant unimum-based aggregation. The proposed neuron dynamically exhibits conjunctive (AND), disjunctive (OR), or compensatory (COMP) behavior without operator search or manual tuning, and provides an explicit index to inspect the logical regime of each rule. Based on this formulation, two evolving neuro-fuzzy classifiers are proposed and evaluated under a prequential protocol on real and synthetic data streams with concept drift. Experimental results show that the proposed models achieve predictive performance statistically comparable to state-of-the-art evolving fuzzy systems, while maintaining a compact rule base, zero numerical instabilities, and interpretable fuzzy rules. An ablation study further confirms the relevance of automatic connective selection across diverse scenarios.

title: From invoices to insights : feature engineering strategies for multilingual product classification in medical device procurement
abstract: This thesis tackles automated multilingual product classification in multinational medical device procurement, using ForMotion Clinic — a prosthetics and orthotics group operating across the five Nordic countries — as a case study. The core problem is that each subsidiary uses its own item codes and languages, so without a shared classification there is no ground truth for what is bought, at what price, and for what clinical purpose. ISO 9999 is adopted as the target taxonomy, and a label-recovery effort raises usable coverage from 2% (2,817 items, 37 codes) to about 10% (14,334 items, 76 codes), making supervised classification feasible. Traditional ML and LLM-based classification are compared on short (~4.5-word), six-language product descriptions. A feature ladder shows that sentence embeddings combined with vendor and unit cost already reach a weighted F1 of 0.950 at 4-digit ISO (five-country mean), and a single pooled pan-Nordic model raises this to 0.959; leave-one-country-out transfer retains 86–100% of within-country performance, showing that one shared classifier can serve all subsidiaries. For the LLM, retrieval-augmented prompting lifts accuracy from 53% to 91%, while prompt design contributes only ~3 points. The two approaches are complementary — ML offers calibrated confidence (ECE ≤ 0.038), while the LLM provides catalogue-wide coverage including unseen item types, and together form a practical hybrid pipeline for ISO 9999 gap-filling across a multinational catalogue.

title: Beyond human attention: AI-to-AI communication as the next frontier in marketing
abstract: Traditional marketing has long been designed around capturing and sustaining human attention. As digital saturation reaches new heights and consumer decision making becomes increasingly mediated by technology, this paradigm is undergoing significant transformation. The rise of autonomous agents such as artificial intelligence (AI) systems acting on behalf of consumers, businesses and institutions, signals a fundamental shift in approach. Marketing messages are no longer directed primarily at humans but at algorithms and virtual agents making choices on their behalf. This paper explores AI-to-AI communication as the next frontier in marketing. The paper examines the current state of attention-based models and the technological advancements driving this change. It also highlights the accelerating deployment of consumer and enterprise AI agents across some major industries. Benefits of this shift include hyperpersonalisation, streamlined transactions and reduced cognitive burden on human decision makers. Risks include working with algorithmic black boxes, erosion of human trust and the potential concentration of influence among a small set of dominant AI platforms. By framing marketing as an ecosystem where algorithms negotiate, filter and prioritise on behalf of stakeholders, this paper emphasises that organisations must redefine brand strategy for this new reality. Readers can learn about the strategic recommendations for adapting marketing practices in a world where AI agents, not humans, are often the primary audience. This article is also included in The Business & Management Collection which can be accessed at http://hstalks.com/business.

title: EXPLAINABLE AI FRAMEWORK FOR KNOWLEDGE BASED CONCEPTS, METHODS, AND APPLICATIONS
abstract: The increasing complexity of Artificial Intelligence (AI) models has heightened concerns regarding transparency, interpretability, and trust in intelligent systems. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has therefore emerged as a critical research area aimed at making AI decision-making processes more understandable and trustworthy for human users. This chapter introduces a comprehensive knowledge-based XAI framework that combines symbolic reasoning with data-driven techniques to enhance model interpretability across varied application domains. The chapter begins by examining core explainability concepts, including interpretability, transparency, causality, and accountability, which form the foundation of explainable systems. It further explores prominent methodological approaches such as model-agnostic explanation methods, rule-based reasoning, attention mechanisms, and knowledge graph–driven inference. By integrating domain knowledge into the explainability process, the proposed framework improves cognitive alignment between AI systems and users while enhancing reliability and contextual relevance of explanations. Practical implementations of knowledge-based XAI are discussed in key domains including healthcare, finance, autonomous systems, and education. These examples demonstrate how explainable models support ethical AI deployment, improve decision confidence, and foster user trust in high-stakes environments. The chapter also addresses future research challenges, such as achieving an optimal balance between interpretability and predictive performance, establishing standardized evaluation metrics for explainability, and ensuring fairness and accountability in AI-driven decisions.Overall, this work provides a structured and practical foundation for researchers and practitioners aiming to design, evaluate, and deploy robust, knowledge-driven explainable AI systems in real-world settings.

title: ARCHITECTURAL SYNTHESIS OF GATED RECURRENT UNITS, ADVANCED ATTENTION PARADIGMS, AND HYBRID SEQUENCE FORECASTING FRAMEWORKS
abstract: Sequence modeling and temporal prediction have undergone a profound structural transition, moving from classical parametric frameworks to gated recurrent networks and ultimately to parallelized attention-based paradigms. This paper provides a rigorous and unified technical analysis of three interconnected evolutionary stages in this transition. First, the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) is analyzed in full mathematical depth: its dualgate control equations are derived, the theoretical gate-skipping mechanism for long-range dependency preservation is formally established through boundary analysis, and a structural comparison against vanilla RNNs and LSTMs is developed including parameter counts, convergence speeds, and empirical benchmark results across speech, music, and sequential classification tasks. GRU architectural variants (GRU1, GRU2, GRU3) are derived by systematic input-projection pruning, and the Minimal Gated Unit (MGU) family (Standard, MGU1, MGU2, MGU3) is formally defined with parameter reduction analysis. The Light Gated Recurrent Unit (LiGRU) is analyzed as a reset-gate-free variant employing ReLU and batch normalization. Second, attention mechanisms are formally derived across three paradigms: additive (Bahdanau) attention with its feedforward alignment scoring, three forms of multiplicative (Luong) attention, and Luong’s global versus local attention strategies including the local alignment position prediction. The Scaled Dot-Product Attention of the Transformer is derived with its scaling factor analysis, Multi-Head Attention is formalized, and sinusoidal positional encodings are presented. Efficient attention variants for long sequences (Sparse Attention, Linear Attention) are surveyed. Third, hybrid forecasting architectures are formally developed: the ARIMA-Deep Learning residual stacking framework, the LSTNet parallel recurrent-convolutional-autoregressive structure, and the ES-RNN exponential smoothing integration. A unified synthesis across all three paradigms concludes the paper with quantitative benchmarks and joint selection guidelines.

title: Explainable AI Framework for Clinical Risk Stratification Using Tabular and Text-Derived Medical Features
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology in modern healthcare, particularly in the area of clinical risk stratification. The growing availability of electronic health records (EHRs), clinical notes, laboratory reports, and patient monitoring data has enabled the development of advanced machine learning and deep learning systems capable of predicting adverse clinical outcomes with improved accuracy. Traditional predictive models have primarily relied on structured tabular medical data such as demographics, laboratory values, and physiological measurements. However, a significant portion of clinically relevant information exists within unstructured textual records, including physician notes, discharge summaries, radiology reports, and nursing documentation. Recent advances in natural language processing (NLP) and multimodal learning have enabled the integration of both tabular and text-derived medical features to enhance predictive performance and support precision medicine.

title: A Conjecture on Single-Photon Bidirectional Instantaneous Communication via Möbius Topological Flows Based on SRE Dynamics
abstract: Modern quantum communication protocols, primarily utilizing quantum key distribution (QKD) derived from entanglement states, are fundamentally bounded by the No-communication Theorem and the inherent stochasticity of wave-function collapse. Consequently, they operate under probabilistic constraints and suffer from physical bottlenecks such as decoherence and low capture efficiency. This paper proposes a deterministic, single-channel, full-duplex communication conjecture rooted in the Status-Relational Entropy (SRE) Dynamics framework, utilizing the open-ended Moebius relational state structure of light. By employing a highly coherent laser as the foundational causal resonance master source, macroscopic physical frequency is redefined as a joint bilateral information coupling density. Utilizing first-order closed-form solutions of the eigenspace and Random Matrix Theory (RMT) heuristic sieves, we construct a "Bidirectional Topological Flow Density Subtractor" algorithm. Theoretical derivations demonstrate that by co-modulating the topological configuration of electromagnetic crystals at both boundaries, deterministic full-duplex signaling can be achieved instantaneously within a single causal chain channel. This framework establishes a novel topological path toward high-efficiency, deterministic communication systems that transcend traditional probabilistic communication limits. Notice on Axiomatic Framework Alignment (SRE v1.5.1):To reconcile traditional relativistic and quantum-mechanical boundaries, all operational derivations and analytical boundaries established in this text - specifically regarding instantaneous full-duplex decoupling and single-photon statistical expectations - strictly inherit the non-Euclidean random-access indexing and causal logic depth lemmas formally proven in SRE Dynamics v1.5.1.

title: The Ladder of Gaps Information C; The Stability Ladder and Deep Learning Generalization– An Axiomatic Derivation from Information Conservation to Generalization Gap
abstract: This paper systematically applies the stability ladder axiomatic system to thetheory of deep learning generalization. Starting from two underlying assumptions—information conservation and the locality of gradient updates—it proves that deepnetwork training must be accompanied by a strictly positive generalization gap inthe loss landscape. The core argument shows that if there is no energy barrierbetween the true solution basin and the overfitting solution basin, then stochasticgradient noise inevitably drives the model into a degenerate attractor that memorizes noise, thereby destroying data structure distinguishability. By introducing adynamic effective coarse-graining description of the loss landscape and an operational definition of basins based on information compression, the generalization gapis re-established as a geometric necessity arising from the separation of scales between representation learning and parameter optimization, rather than an accidental product of specific architectures or regularization techniques. The frameworkfurther establishes strict dual relationships with PAC learning, neural tangent kernel theory, and the lottery ticket hypothesis, and provides quantitative predictionsfor implicit regularization techniques. This theory reconstructs the generalizationability of deep learning from an empirical phenomenon to be explained into thelogical output of a self-consistent axiomatic system.

title: Continuous Waveform Analysis of Offshore DAS Arrays for Automatic Earthquake Detection and Magnitude Estimation in the UKCS
abstract: A reliable, long-term seismic monitoring system near the large-scale carbon storage areas recently licensed in the North Sea and other offshore areas in the UK and other countries in northern Europe, is essential to guarantee safe injection and storage operations. In offshore areas, permanent seismic monitoring systems could either be based in nearby monitoring wells and/or on conventional ocean bottom seismometer arrays. Alternatively, offshore DAS arrays could provide a more cost-effective seismic monitoring solution. In this study, we assess the passive waveform dataset recorded continuously for one month by an offshore DAS array in the UK Southern North Sea operated by Tampnet, to automatically detect and characterise seismic events. This DAS array is located just south of some carbon storage areas recently licensed by the UK NSTA, making it suitable for long-term monitoring of CO2 injection once the injection wells are fully operational in the following years.

title: BiLSTM-ResNet-CRF: An Improved Model for Subject Knowledge Graph Construction
abstract: The emergence of massive knowledge in online learning systems has increased the difficulty for learners to acquire the necessary information. Due to unclear information expression and excessive knowledge redundancy, learners face challenges in identifying relevant knowledge. Furthermore, the presence of substantial unstructured knowledge in subject domains also hinders the effective transmission and application of knowledge. To address these issues, a framework for constructing a subject domain knowledge graph is proposed in this work. The framework primarily aims to visualize isolated information and connect knowledge into graph structures. The knowledge graph can help learners quickly and efficiently acquire the knowledge they need. The novel framework is constructed with three steps. The first step is to design the ontology rules based on the domain-specific subject knowledge from the perspective of classification, and also to construct the schema layer of the knowledge graph. The second step is to propose a domain-optimized BiLSTM-ResNet-CRF model for subject domain entity recognition, which introduces residual blocks to enhance fine-grained local contextual feature extraction for multi-word technical terms, addressing the limitations of traditional BiLSTM-CRF models in educational text processing. The BERT relation extraction model is used to extract relations between knowledge entities. Then the data layer is constructed. Finally, the third step is to achieve knowledge fusion through entity linking and two-layer entity alignment against results stored in a database. The result comparisons on the dataset show that the novel BiLSTM-ResNet-CRF model has higher scores than several other classical models, achieving an F1-score of 80.26%. The proposed framework’s effectiveness is rigorously validated using high school mathematics as a representative case study with a well-structured knowledge system.

title: AI και ηγεσία: o ρόλος των manager στην εποχή της Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης
abstract: Η παρούσα εργασία εξετάζει διεξοδικά τον ρόλο της τεχνητής νοημοσύνης στη σύγχρονη διοίκηση των επιχειρήσεων, με ιδιαίτερη έμφαση στη λήψη αποφάσεων, στη στρατηγική διοίκηση και στην ηγεσία. Μέσω συστηματικής βιβλιογραφικής ανασκόπησης και εφαρμογής της μεθοδολογίας PRISMA, αναλύονται επιστημονικές μελέτες που αναδεικνύουν τις κύριες διαστάσεις εφαρμογής της τεχνητής νοημοσύνης και τις τεχνολογίες που αξιοποιούνται στο σύγχρονο διοικητικό περιβάλλον. Τα ευρήματα υποδεικνύουν εμφατικά ότι η τεχνητή νοημοσύνη ενισχύει την επιχειρησιακή αποτελεσματικότητα, βελτιώνει την ποιότητα των αποφάσεων και συμβάλλει στην ανάπτυξη καινοτόμων στρατηγικών. Ταυτοχρόνως, αναδεικνύονται σημαντικές προκλήσεις που σχετίζονται με ζητήματα διαφάνειας, ηθικής και διαχείρισης δεδομένων. Η εργασία καταλήγει στο συμπέρασμα ότι η επιτυχής ενσωμάτωση της τεχνητής νοημοσύνης προϋποθέτει συνδυασμό τεχνολογικής κατανόησης, διοικητικής ικανότητας και επιχειρησιακή προσαρμοστικότητας.

Μέσω συστηματικής βιβλιογραφικής ανασκόπησης και εφαρμογής της μεθοδολογίας PRISMA, αναλύονται επιστημονικές μελέτες που αναδεικνύουν τις κύριες διαστάσεις εφαρμογής της τεχνητής νοημοσύνης και τις τεχνολογίες που αξιοποιούνται στο σύγχρονο διοικητικό περιβάλλον. Τα ευρήματα υποδεικνύουν εμφατικά ότι η τεχνητή νοημοσύνη ενισχύει την επιχειρησιακή αποτελεσματικότητα, βελτιώνει την ποιότητα των αποφάσεων και συμβάλλει στην ανάπτυξη καινοτόμων στρατηγικών. Ταυτοχρόνως, αναδεικνύονται σημαντικές προκλήσεις που σχετίζονται με ζητήματα διαφάνειας, ηθικής και διαχείρισης δεδομένων. Η εργασία καταλήγει στο συμπέρασμα ότι η επιτυχής ενσωμάτωση της τεχνητής νοημοσύνης προϋποθέτει συνδυασμό τεχνολογικής κατανόησης, διοικητικής ικανότητας και επιχειρησιακή προσαρμοστικότητας.
evidence.venue: University of Peloponnese

title: Beyond e-learning in the age of artificial intelligence
abstract: Organizational upskilling needs are rising, yet traditional e-Learning is time-consuming and poorly suited to the rapidly evolving needs of knowledge workers, such as sales engineers in information technology. This convergent mixed-methods study compared a course assisted by a generative pedagogical conversational agent (GenPCA) with a traditional e-Learning course, measuring assessment scores, learner-perceived universal design for learning (UDL) expression, and development cost efficiency. Grounded in UDL and mind, brain, and education science, this study situates the results within Benjamin Bloom's 2-sigma problem. Forty-five sales engineers completed the course, a knowledge posttest, and a postsurvey of Likert-scale and open-ended items, with development time tracked for each modality. Quantitative data were analyzed using t tests, Cohen's d effect sizes, and Mann-Whitney U tests, and the instrument's reliability was confirmed with Cronbach's alpha and Spearman-Brown. The qualitative data were analyzed through two-cycle coding, with the strands merged during interpretation. Assessment scores did not differ between the groups. Both cohorts arrived with prior expertise, and their scores clustered near the top of the instrument. This ceiling effect compressed the between-group variance, restricting the range needed to detect relationships among UDL perceptions, GenPCA didactical factors, and outcomes, so the null findings were traced to a single boundary condition. UDL expression favored the GenPCA modality, with large effect sizes across all three UDL networks: engagement, representation, and action-expression. Development effort favored GenPCA, requiring 8 hr against 119 hr for the traditional build, a roughly 15-fold reduction for this single course. Three contributions extend the work, including the inductive finding of aspirational convergence, a shared aspiration of learning affordances voiced across both modalities, the framing of the ceiling effect as a boundary condition on Bloom's 2-sigma, and the UDL-GenPCA Experience Inventory, a prototype instrument of UDL and GenPCA didactical factors with strong internal consistency. The GenPCA modality showed greater expression and required less development time. The assessment comparison remained inconclusive because the ceiling effect rendered any true difference statistically invisible. That boundary condition applies to tenured engineers with foundational content, not the earlier-career practitioners who stand to gain the most. Designing and measuring for those learners is the work this study leaves to the field. Keywords: generative pedagogical conversational agents, universal design for learning, workplace learning, sales engineers, Bloom's 2-sigma problem.

title: Hybrid Semantic Intelligence Dataset for AI-Generated and Human-Authored Research Abstract Analysis
abstract: This dataset contains AI research abstracts collected from publicly available research repositories, publication platforms, and Large Language Model (LLM)-generated scientific content sources. The dataset was constructed to support research in semantic intelligence, topic modeling, clustering, and AI-generated text analysis. The corpus consists of two categories of research abstracts: (1) LLM-generated scientific abstracts and (2) human-authored AI research abstracts. The original dataset contains 4,000 research abstracts, including: - 2,000 LLM-generated abstracts (Label = 0) - 2,000 human-authored abstracts (Label = 1) The dataset was collected through web scraping and manual curation, followed by preprocessing operations including duplicate removal, lowercase normalization, punctuation filtering, URL removal, stopword elimination, and token cleaning. After duplicate removal, the final processed corpus contains 3,989 semantically valid research abstracts. Dataset Statistics: - Original Dataset Size: 4,000 abstracts - Final Processed Corpus: 3,989 abstracts - Number of Classes: 2 - Language: English - Labels: - 0 = LLM-generated abstracts - 1 = Human-authored abstracts The dataset is suitable for multiple Natural Language Processing (NLP) and semantic intelligence tasks, including: - Semantic clustering - Topic modeling - AI-generated text analysis - Semantic drift analysis - NLP representation learning - Interpretable semantic analysis - Transformer-based text mining - Scientific document analysis This dataset was developed as part of the research study: “Hybrid Semantic Intelligence Framework for AI-Generated and Human-Authored Research Abstract Analysis.”

title: Is Hallucination Not a Flaw? The Psychological Code of AI Hallucination Shaping Brand Attitudes
abstract: AI hallucination is traditionally viewed as a technical defect, yet its creative potential in brand communication remains underexplored. This study investigates how AI hallucination influences consumers’ brand attitudes in image advertising and identifies boundary conditions. An experiment with 398 participants reveals that factual hallucination negatively affects brand attitude, whereas creative hallucination exerts a positive effect. Artificial empathy and psychological distance serially mediate these effects, and media literacy plays a dual moderating role. The findings enrich theories of AI hallucination and consumer behavior while offering actionable guidance for brands employing generative AI in advertising. Keywords: AI Hallucination, Psychology Distance, Brand Attitude, Source Characteristics

title: HyperFond: A Transparent and Post-Quantum Distributed SNARK with Polylogarithmic Communication
abstract: Recent years have witnessed the surge of academic researches and industrial implementations of succinct non-interactive arguments of knowledge (SNARKs). However, proving time remains a bottleneck for applying SNARKs to large-scale circuits. To accelerate the proof generation process, a promising way is to distribute the workload to several machines running in parallel, the SNARKs with which feature are called distributed SNARKs. Nevertheless, most existing works either require a trusted setup, or rely on quantum-insecure assumptions, or suffer from linear communication costs.
